findings.summary: The residual panel's x axis is drawn to active-set trip 15 while the plotted trajectory ends at trip 4 in frame 146 (and trip 12-13 in frame 137). Most of the panel is empty and the handful of real points are squeezed into its left third, halving the horizontal resolution a reader has for the trip-1 rise the frame-146 argument depends on.

The EFIT label flux contours are drawn in a very light grey, hard to follow against white and noticeably fainter than the blue solved flux. Where the two fields interleave in the poloidal panel, the reference field a reader must compare against is the harder one to trace.

The EFIT label flux and the bounding-boundary reference are the lightest marks on the page while the caption's argument is a comparison against them; the recessive styling makes the reference reading effortful at the rendered size.

The poloidal panel occupies roughly a seventh of the canvas width, so the contours, limiter outline and null markers the figure exists to show are the smallest elements on the page, subordinate to the legend and to the largely empty residual axis.

notes: Both figures were judged only from the rendered PNGs named in the node: image-0.png is frame 137 (the frame that holds its plasma) and image-1.png is frame 146 (the frame that loses it). No SVG was opened, read, listed, searched, rendered or diffed.

The reviewed head 00105c532e16 changes only docs/evidence/fragments/diiid-vertical-force-balance/diiid-frame-146-vertical-loss.html relative to its predecessor 4c40f2138e44; the two PNGs are unchanged by that commit, so the rendered images reviewed are the run's current artifacts.
Findings are anchored to the figure's repository path, or to the line of the drawing script the run reuses where the defect is in that script; no finding is anchored to SVG markup.
No blocking defect was found: no label is clipped or overlapping in either figure, and every caption, legend entry and axis label is readable at the rendered size.
This is a read-only figure review. No figure, caption or script was edited, created, moved, deleted or reformatted.
